## Continuum and soft bodies: independence from the mesh

Soft robots and compliant links are modelled by finite elements, where the number of
coordinates is a numerical choice. A sound information measure must converge as the mesh
is refined.

::: {#thm-mesh name="Mesh independence"}
Let a linear elastic body be semi-discretized by conforming finite elements, with
consistent mass $H_N$ and stiffness $K_N$, and let $u_N(t)$ be the finite-element field. Then the
energy-whitened Gram is
$$
  G_N^{ij}=\gamma\sum_k\Big[a\big(u^i_{N,k},u^j_{N,k}\big)+m\big(\dot u^i_{N,k},\dot u^j_{N,k}\big)\Big],
$$
where $a(\cdot,\cdot)$ is the continuum strain-energy bilinear form and $m(\cdot,\cdot)$ the
continuum kinetic-energy (mass) form. Suppose the finite-element solutions converge in the
energy norm at each sample time. This is classical for semi-discrete approximations of
damped second-order hyperbolic problems with sufficiently regular data
[@dupont1973l2; @baker1976error; @geveci1984convergence]; we *assume* it here. Then
$G_N\to G_\infty$ and the bits converge.

By contrast, per-node isotropic noise has Gram entries
$\approx\frac{N}{L}\times(L^2\text{ inner product})$. It grows linearly in $N$, so by
@prp-snr(b) the bits grow like $\frac r2\log_2N$: about $\frac r2$ bits per mesh
doubling.
:::

::: {.proof}
*The identity.* With $u_N=\sum_iU_i\psi_i$ in the nodal basis, the finite-element
matrices are defined by $U^\top K_NU'=a(u_N,u_N')$ and $\dot U^\top H_N\dot U'=m(\dot
u_N,\dot u_N')$. Substituting into @eq-gram with $C^\top C=\Em_N$ gives the
displayed identity. The nodes have disappeared: the Gram is a sum of *continuum*
energy inner products of the finite-element fields.

*Convergence.* Each entry is a finite sum (over finitely many $k$) of inner products,
which are continuous in the energy norm. So energy-norm convergence of each field implies
convergence of each entry. Then apply continuity of $\log\det(I+\cdot)$.

*The per-node estimate.* For a uniform mesh of spacing $h=L/N$ and smooth fields,
$\sum_iU_iU_i'\approx h^{-1}\int uu'\,dx$, a Riemann sum.
:::

::: {#rem-auto-3 name="Cylindrical noise is harmless here"}
In the continuum limit, isotropic noise in energy coordinates is white noise on the energy
Hilbert space. That is a cylindrical measure, not a countably additive one. It does no
harm here: the signal $\{Mw\}$ spans at most $d$ dimensions, and @lem-gauss shows
that the information depends only on the $d\times d$ matrix $M^\top M$. This is the
noise-side counterpart of the requirement, stressed in function-space Bayesian inversion,
that priors and inner products be defined so as to survive refinement:

- MCMC proposals that are robust under mesh refinement
    [@cotter2013mcmc];
- finite-element inner products weighted by the mass matrix
    [@buithanh2013computational, Sec. 3.3];
- see also @stuart2010inverse.

:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Numerical check"}
A fixed-free axial rod (length 0.2 m, $EA=10^3$ N, $\rho A=0.1$ kg/m, so the
first mode is at 125 Hz) with consistent mass, stiffness-proportional damping and a tip
force ($B_w=400$ Hz, $d=68$), for $N=2,\dots,128$ elements (@fig-rod,
`check_rod`):

- energy-whitened bits converge, $297.93\to302.109$, changing by $0.004$ between
    $N=64$ and $128$;
- per-node isotropic bits grow by $33.2$ bits per doubling, against
    $\frac r2=34$ predicted;
- the tip's motion alone also converges, which shows that the problem is noise *per
    coordinate*, not discretization.

:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-rod
#| fig-cap: |
#|   Mesh refinement of a finite-element rod. Energy whitening gives a mesh-independent
#|   answer. Per-node noise is the double-counting artifact of @prp-dup at scale: every
#|   refinement adds "free second looks."
from mibook import figures
figures.fig_rod();
```

## Gear ratios and transmission design

Relabelling a motor angle on the input side of a gear as an angle on the output side is a
reparametrization: $T=\diag(1,1/N)$ in the SEA layout. By @thm-invariance,
energy-whitened bits do not move. Per-coordinate bits jump from 81.37 to 130.91 bits
(@fig-invariance).

*Changing* the gear ratio is a different matter: it changes the reflected inertia
$N^2I_{\rm rot}$, which is a physical change in $H$. That change enters $\Em$, and it
correctly changes the bits. The energy metric separates bookkeeping from design, which is
what a sweep over rotor inertia (such as Table I of @patterson2026quantifying) needs.

## Floating bases: when a singular metric loses nothing {#sec-floating}

For an unclamped leg or a free-flying quadruped, $K$ is singular: rigid-body
*positions* store no energy, while $H\succ0$ still weighs velocities. The
whitening map $\Em^{1/2}$, with eigenvalues clipped at zero by `sym_sqrt`, is
blind to zero-energy positions. Does that lose information?

::: {#prp-floating name="No loss when force and ground share the Jacobian"}
Suppose:

(i) $K\succeq k_iJ^\top J$ with $k_i>0$, where $J$ is the Jacobian through which the
    unknown force acts;
(ii) $D\phi=0$ for every $\phi\in\ker K$. Physically, internal and ground dampers act
    only on relative or foot motion.

Then, from rest, the trajectory never enters $\ker K$. More precisely, $\phi^\top Hq(t)=0$
for all $\phi\in\ker K$ and all $t$. On the subspace where the motion lives, $\Em$ is
positive definite, so nothing is lost.
:::

::: {.proof}
*Step 1: zero-energy modes are not forced.* For $\phi\in\ker K$,
$0=\phi^\top K\phi\ge k_i(J\phi)^2$, so $J\phi=0$.

*Step 2: their coordinates stay at zero.* Let $\eta=\phi^\top Hq$. Multiply
@eq-eom on the left by $\phi^\top$:
$$
  \ddot\eta=(J\phi)^\top f-(D\phi)^\top\dot q-(K\phi)^\top q=0 .
$$
With $\eta(0)=\dot\eta(0)=0$, we get $\eta\equiv0$.

*Step 3: $\Em$ is definite on the motion.* By Step 2, $q(t)$ lies in the
$H$-orthogonal complement of $\ker K$. Any nonzero $q$ in that complement is not in
$\ker K$, so $q^\top Kq>0$ there.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Numerical check"}
On the analysis library's free bench (trunk plus leg, $q=(y_b,\theta)$), the
energy metric and the kinetic metric ($\omega_{\rm ref}^2H$ in the position block) give
the same bits,
71.709.

The equality has a reason: the motion lives on $\mathrm{span}(H^{-1}J^\top)$. On
that line, $K$ restricts to $k_i(JH^{-1}J^\top)^2$ and $H$ restricts to $JH^{-1}J^\top$.
Their ratio is $k_i/m_e=\omega_{\rm ref}^2$, where $m_e$ is the effective mass at the foot,
so the two metrics agree on the motion.

A counterexample violates (i) by pushing on the trunk instead of the foot. The zero mode
is then forced ($\phi_0^\top e_1=-0.17$), and the singular metric loses
$71.86-49.66=22.2$ bits relative to the regularized one (`check_floating`).
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="What this means physically"}
The quadruped experiments of @patterson2026quantifying [Sec. V] apply random pushes
$w_{\rm ext}$ to the calves of a floating quadruped. Those pushes do excite zero-stiffness base positions, so an energy metric built
from joint springs alone would discard base-position information. Three remedies:

1. keep the base velocities (always weighted, since $H\succ0$) and accept that base
    position is gauge;
2. regularize the position block with $\omega_{\rm ref}^2H$ (the kinetic
    metric, `"kinetic"` in the code) and report sensitivity to $\omega_{\rm ref}$;
3. use the potential of gravity and contact springs at the operating point.

The Zahedi-Ay $\mathrm{MC}_W$ of @sec-mcw has no Gibbs law when $\Em$ is singular,
which is why `morphological_bits` correctly refuses the free bench.
:::

## Further uses

- *Where information sits in the body.* @def-subset measures how much a part of the
    body holds when the noise belongs to the body, and @fig-shapley splits the SEA's
    information over its coordinates. The research note on
    [information propagation](../notes/2026-11-21-information-propagation.qmd) asks the
    same question under thermal noise.
- *Variable-stiffness and parallel-elastic actuators, compliant feet.* All of
    these add or remove coordinates as parameters vary. @thm-limit guarantees
    continuity across the degenerate limits.
- *Learned estimators.* For InfoNCE, whitening does not change the true
    information (@lem-noise(a)), but it gives the critic dimensionally
    homogeneous inputs in $\sqrt{\mathrm J}$. Per-feature $z$-scoring is a
    data-dependent diagonal metric: it is not basis-free, and it changes with the
    force prior. Noise must be added *after* whitening, as `sim_info` does.
